1. The purpose of this memo is to give guidance to decision makers (DM) on The Social Security 
(Scotland) Act 2018 (Disability Assistance) (Consequential Amendments) Order 2025
1
. The amendments 
will come into force on 21.3.25.

2. This order
1
 
makes changes to social security legislation to reflect the introduction by the Scottish 
Government (SG) of the Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance (SADLA). SADLA will

1. 
replace DLA for current DLA claimants who are over the age of 18 and are resident in Scotland 
and

2. 
operate broadly the same way as DLA so those in receipt will have the same access to additional 
amounts and exemptions in reserved benefits as those in receipt of DLA.

Additional amount for the severely disabled

30. An award of SPC may include an additional amount for persons who are severely disabled. SADLA is 
added to the list of qualifying benefits when considering whether the claimant or, if applicable, any 
partner, is severely disabled.
1

31. When considering whether members of a polygamous marriage are entitled to an additional amount 
for persons who are severely disabled, SADLA is added to the list of qualifying benefits when considering 
whether a claimant, any partner and any additional spouse is severely disabled.
1

32. For the purposes of calculating housing costs, a non-dependant deduction should not be made where 
the claimant or a partner is in receipt of the care component of SADLA
1
.

33. When calculating a non-dependent’s gross weekly income, SADLA is added to the list of benefits 
that are disregarded
1

BACKDATING CLAIMS FOR A RELEVANT BENEFIT

36. For the purposes of the rules on backdating claims for a relevant benefit after the award of a 
qualifying benefit in DMG 02260, SADLA is a “qualifying benefit”
1
 
from 21.3.25.
37. After 28 days in hospital or a care home, the amount of SADLA reduces to nil. where

1.
 as a result of the SADLA reducing to nil, an award of a relevant benefit (DMG 02263) has been 
terminated or reduced, or payment has ceased; 
and

2.1
. on revision, supersession, or appeal
 or

2.2
. because the claimant has left hospital or the care home 
and

3.
 the relevant benefit is claimed again within three months of the date on which a decision to 
restore SADLA was made.

The new claim for the relevant benefit can be treated as made on the date in paragraph 38
1
.

38. Where the provisions in paragraph 37 are satisfied, the new claim for the relevant benefit
 
is treated 
as made on

1.
 the date from which the previous award of the relevant benefit was terminated 
or

2.
 the date from which SADLA increases to more than nil

39. The definition of ‘Scottish disability benefit’ for revision and supersession purposes
1
 has been 
amended so that it now includes SADLA. See further guidance in paragraphs 40 to 48.
Supersession of a SPC award because of entitlement to SADLA

1.
 
an award of SPC is superseded on the ground that there has been a relevant change of 
circumstances since the award took effect
 
and

2.
 
the change of circumstances is that the claimant or partner has become entitled to
 
SADLA

the superseding decision takes effect from the beginning of the benefit week in which the first day of 
the new SADLA entitlement falls or, if that is not practicable, on the first day of the following benefit 
week
1

from which the relevant benefit has been awarded

the award of the relevant benefit can be revised.

43. The regulations
1
 
have also been amended to include new rules for IS supersessions carried out 
because SADLA has been reduced or increased as a result of short periods in or out of a hospital or care 
home. See further guidance in paragraph 44.

1.
 an IS award is superseded on the ground that a relevant change of circumstances has occurred 
and

2.1
 SADLA has been reduced or increased for less than a week because the claimant has 
been admitted to a hospital or care home
 or

2.1
 SADLA has been increased for less than a week because the claimant has left a hospital 
or care home

the superseding decision takes effect from the actual day on which the claimant entered or left the 
hospital or care home
1
.

SADLA

45. The regulations
1
 have also been amended to include a new rule for SPC supersessions
 
carried out 
because SADLA has been awarded.

1.
 an SPC award is superseded on the ground that a relevant change of circumstances has 
occurred 
and

2.
 the change is the claimant or partner has become entitled to the SADLA care component at the 
middle or higher rate

the superseding decision take effects on the first day of the SPC benefit week in which that change 
occurs, or if that is not practicable in the circumstances of the case, on the first day of the next following 
benefit week
1
.

ESA supersession for entering or leaving a care home, hospital or legal detention for less than a week
47. The regulations
1 
have also been amended to include new rules for ESA supersessions
 
carried out 
because SADLA has been reduced or increased as a result of short periods in or out of a hospital, care 
home or legal detention. See guidance in paragraph 48.

1. 
an ESA award is superseded on the ground that a relevant change of circumstances has 
occurred
 and

2.1
 SADLA has been reduced or increased for less than a week because the claimant has 
been admitted to a hospital or care home 
or

2.1
 SADLA has been reduced to nil or increased from nil for less than a week under the 
special SADLA rules for persons who have transferred to another part of the UK and are in 
hospital, a care home or legal detention

the superseding decision takes effect from the actual day on which the claimant entered or left hospital, 
care home or legal detention
1
